### Candidate: James Heward — Head of Architecture (marked 2026-10-12)

**Trigger (why now).** In the nine days to 12 Oct 2026, Scott Logic created a company-wide architecture discipline: new `Principal Architect` postings in Edinburgh, Bristol and Newcastle, and every `Solutions Architect` role re-filed from `Development` to `Architecture`. Heward leads that practice; the build-out is happening on his watch.

**The event.** Scott Logic's public calendar now carries the FINOS Q4 All Community Call (21 Oct) and the FINOS Fall 2026 Hackathon (13 Nov), plus an open-source-security risk session. The content trail is his: the YouTube series on agentic governance — *Setting up robust governance for agentic AI*, *Data foundations for agentic AI*, *How AI has changed the economics of modernisation*, *How to deploy agentic AI safely and at scale*, *Laying the foundations for agentic AI* — and the 14 Aug blog *AI success depends on data foundations*.

**Architecture role across the company.** Firm-wide architecture practice; `Principal Architect` band now in Edinburgh, Bristol and Newcastle; architecture carved out as its own discipline rather than a Development sub-track.

**Adjacency to our cause.** His published positions are governance, data foundations and the economics of modernisation for agentic AI in regulated settings — the cognatability / regulated-agentic-AI territory. He is not selling against us; he is describing the problem we build the evidence base for (the intent repository as the layer that makes his "foundations" auditable; the AI Act oversight duty as the forcing function).

**Approach vectors.**
1. *Content-first (recommended).* Engage substantively on his governance/agentic videos and the data-foundations post before any direct approach — same discipline as Eberhardt. Comment, don't pitch.
2. *Capability / subcontract.* The Principal Architect build-out is senior-end capacity pressure; a specialist (intent architecture, regulated agentic governance) is the natural adjacent buy. Grey is the contracting door; Heward is the technical one.
3. *Event.* The FINOS Fall Hackathon (13 Nov) and Q4 Community Call (21 Oct) are open, on-theme and Scott Logic-attended — low-stakes in-person ground.
4. *Referral.* Sam Perridge (AI Runway) and Suzanne Angell (legacy modernisation content) are internal amplifiers; Heward is the technical decision-maker.

**Content to prepare (signal-as-proof).** A substantive response to *three foundations for agentic AI in Financial Services* / the governance videos, on the practitioner register:

> *"Your three foundations assume the intent is written down somewhere a regulator can read. In most regulated shops it isn't — it lives in a head or a ticket queue. The intent repository is the layer that makes your foundations auditable; the AI Act oversight duty is what forces it. How are you handling that at Scott Logic?"*

That keeps to the outreach playbook's shape: one observation, no capability claim, end with a question.

## How to Use This Map

1. **Recon engine detects a signal** (e.g., "Scott Logic posted a new blog about coding agent safety" or "Waracle appointed a new Chief AI Officer")
2. **Consult this map** to identify the right person to contact
3. **Craft outreach** referencing the specific observed signal — not a cold pitch
4. **Update this map** when contacts change roles, leave, or new contacts are identified

This map is maintained by hand. It is NOT automated. The recon engine's job is to tell you *when* to act; this map tells you *who* to act on.
